lore: A normal Unicorn was once trotting through the serene forests of Silverglade, when something horrific happened. A group of curious minds decided to test the limits of flammability using hag-brewed accelerants, borrowed Fey fire magic, and a very large Bunsen burner courtesy of Sparkgrinder. The result was a Unicorn that not only caught fire, not only stayed on fire, but somehow managed to remain alive.

Known now as the Blazicorn, the poor creature continues to exist while blazing like a festive torch. It is actually quite impressive given that most creatures, when exposed to this amount of heat, either turn to dust or a roast dinner. Today, the Blazicorn trots through Silverglade with bright flaming hooves and a mane that crackles cheerfully, leaving behind singed grass, burnt trees, and - initially at least - some very confused Elves.

Who created the Blazicorn? Turns out it was nobody special - just a bunch of engineers and mages who wondered ‘what if’. To this day the Blazicorn is both a monument and a reminder. A monument to the fact that a bunch of curious nerds can do a huge amount of damage in a very short amount of time. And a reminder that sometimes all of us should really ignore our intrusive thoughts.

lore: Cinderpelt was once an ordinary she-wolf living a peaceful life near the Underworld Gate in Maugrim Woods. But everything changed when Vulcanus began poking holes between realms, causing strange transformations across Krystara. One morning Cinderpelt simply burst into flame, which was a surprise to everyone, especially her.

Burning is not something wolves are typically known for. What surprised Cinderpelt more than the fact she was on fire, was that there were options beyond jumping in a river or becoming a roast wolf - there was rage. The blaze replaced her calm nature with a raw manic fury. She now races through the woods in alternating fits of anger and panic, leaving a trail of scorched undergrowth and barbecued squirrels behind her.

At one point, Cinderpelt accidentally set half of a Wargare hunting camp alight as she ran frantically through it. The hunters fled in confusion, unsure whether to chase her, shoot her, or find a very large bucket of water. Cinderpelt may not be the only creature changing in this way, but she is certainly the one making the most dramatic entrances and exits.

lore: Sera Ashsong grew up in Pan’s Vale, a kingdom famous for music, merriment, and goats that party far harder than any responsible goat should. She was always cold as a child, so she developed a fondness for fire and songs about fire, which her very sensible parents tried to manage by giving her a ring of fire resistance for her fifth birthday. Sadly, fire resistance does not prevent one from catching alight, as Sera eventually proved in spectacular fashion.

At the age of ten Sera stumbled across a secret coven of Infernus-worshipping Satyrs, who lived life on the edge by collecting equally fiery goats… and explosives. They also liked to sing. She listened and learned. Sera only meant to chant those songs quietly to herself - to keep warm on cold nights, but curiosity is a powerful force in a young pyromaniac. And one day she wondered if the Wild Queen’s palace might catch fire…

The answer turned out to be no, but not because it wasn't flammable. It was because Sera accidentally summoned a fire elemental directly on top of herself, instead of on top of the palace. Their two spirits merged together, turning Sera into a living blaze. The building survived, and so did a rather fiery Sera, but she has remained that way ever since. At least she is never cold now, which would be a great outcome except that nobody ever invites her over for dinner.

lore: Emberpetal is a Fire Dryad. Bound to her tree, she spends her days keeping it lively and just a little bit magical. Her tree is a Flame Tree, a rare marvel whose leaves glow bright red through most of the year and whose pale bark warms the winter air. When the Flame Tree sheds its leaves, Emberpetal glows softly too, keeping herself and her tree snug through the cold months.

Just like her Flame Tree, Emberpetal can store sunlight in the warmer months and release it as gentle flames when the world grows chilly. This makes her both a comfort and a hazard, depending on how close one stands and how flammable one happens to be. The Wood Elves pretend to be unimpressed, but they give her plenty of space because the unknown is much scarier when it is on fire.

Any ‘respect’ being shown may also be because a group of snooty Wood Elves once tried to lecture Emberpetal about the dangers of forest fires. Her response was to grow warmer and warmer until the elves scrambled up nearby trees in alarm with pants ablaze. She found the whole thing delightful and still insists it was a perfectly reasonable response to being patronized.

lore: The Bloodstone Dragon was once an ordinary red dragon soaring over Dragon’s Claw, proud, fiery, and very difficult to safely annoy. Its fate changed however when it strayed too close to Hellcrag in the early days of the Stone Curse, which crystallized its blood. A normal creature would have perished, but a dragon’s heart is stubborn, and it kept pumping until the strange new blood found a way to work.

The Bloodstone Dragon’s crystalline blood is both a curse and a blessing, as it turns every wound the Dragon suffers into clusters of blood red rubies on its skin. Over the centuries these clusters have grown into a full suit of glittering armour, making the dragon look like it is wearing its own hoard. The rubies are tough, sharp, and… valuable.

Having spotted a ‘pile of rubies’ in a cave, a band of treasure hunters once accidentally ambushed the Dragon, only to realise the treasure they sought was actually just about to toast and eat them. When it flew away from this breakfast buffet, the Bloodstone Dragon had shed a few more rubies, and was looking even more valuable than before. Today it is hunted wherever it goes, not because it is feared, but because it is worth a fortune, which the dragon finds both very rude and very flattering.

lore: Hellfire Ballistas began as ordinary siege engines in Hellcrag before the Petrification Curse swept across the kingdom and turned everything to stone. One unlucky ballista happened to be on fire at the exact moment the curse was cast, which resulted in a blazing stone siege engine that refused to go out. This accidental marvel became the prototype for all future Hellfire Ballistas.

A Hellfire Balista can fire six flaming bolts at once, which is excellent for picking dragons out of the sky. A dragon can dodge one bolt, but six is a much harder negotiation. The addition of a portal to the Fire Plane keeps the whole contraption burning nicely and ensures every bolt is toasty warm and ready to inflict maximum pyrotechnic mayhem.

In the years since their invention Hellfire Ballistas seem to have developed some amount of sentience. When a squad of Hellcrag engineers attempted to extinguish one for study, the ballista responded by firing all six bolts straight upward. The engineers regarded this behavior curiously - for approximately 16 seconds, after which the bolts landed, skewering them all. Since then, all of Hellcrag has agreed that Hellfire Ballistas are best studied or admired from a very safe distance.

lore: Hell Trolls were once ordinary Trolls living in the Blighted Lands before Daemons burst into Krystara during the terrible event known as the Blight. Trolls regenerated quickly, which made them annoyingly difficult for the Daemons to kill, since a Troll could be beaten, skewered, and squashed but then get back up and knock the Daemonic snot out of you. After this happened several times, the Daemons learned that fire stopped Trolls from regenerating, which seemed like a great solution… at first.

Trolls - of all kinds - mutate faster than anyone can reasonably keep track of… a trait likely tied to their rapid regeneration. When the Daemons found a Troll that could regenerate even while on fire, things escalated quickly. Trolls heal fast, but they breed even faster, and soon the mountains were crawling with fireproof Trolls, flaming Trolls, and Trolls that had developed a taste for Daemon giblets. Sometimes all three.

Those lucky Trolls who won the trifecta - now known as Hell Trolls - managed to survive the Daemons’ increasingly desperate attempts to destroy them. Every new method of extermination produced a new kind of Troll, each more troublesome than the last. Eventually the Daemons gave up entirely and left all the Trolls the hell alone, which is probably the closest thing to a successful rebellion the Blighted Lands will ever see.

lore: Vulcanus emerged millennia ago in the Fire Realm as a tiny fire sprite who already wanted to be in charge of absolutely everyone. He made the other sprites line up, march around, and obey his every command, and any failure was met with a swift fistful of magma to the face. As he grew into a towering elemental lord, he decided the wider universe could also benefit from this type of leadership.

While traveling from plane to plane, Vulcanus discovered the Gem Realm, where he found seven Fire Rubies. They were guarded by Gem Dragons who were not prepared for his… ahh… enthusiastic greeting. After immolating the Dragons, he claimed the Fire Rubies and learned they could literally tear down the walls between realms. In a moment of brilliance, he imagined the universe as one giant open-plan workspace where he could be in charge of every living creature in existence.

Vulcanus began this campaign of universal domination with Krystara, a place primed for his particular brand of government - pyrocracy - due to the number of flammable races living there. Having arrived in Broken Spire, he discovered that his long-time-favorite fistful of magma settled most arguments before they even began, leaving him a force to be reckoned with, mostly because nobody wanted to reckon with things while their face was on fire.

lore: Grub Wildshot was born in the ramshackle chaos of Zaejin, where most Goblins learn to run from any blackpowder they see. Grub was built differently though - he liked playing with the powder. Surrounded by noise, smoke, and questionable engineering, he grew up to be a Goblin with a deep and abiding love for guns. By adulthood he owned more firearms than his village militia, and he cherished each one like a loud, dangerous child.

Grub will shoot anything that can launch a projectile, preferably while laughing and not checking which way it is pointed. His favourite gun, Momma, is big, loud, unpredictable, and has broken his jaw three times with its insane recoil, which he insists is a sign of affection, because his mother did the same. Grub carries so much ammunition that his pockets bulge, his pants jingle, and he keeps two explosive shells tucked up his nose for emergencies.

Unfortunately, some years back, Grub developed a sinus infection. One of the resultant sneezes shot one of the shells at a village elder, who exploded like a lump of green jello in a blender with the top left off. This left Grub as the default leader of the village, mostly because nobody wanted to approach the still-sneezing Goblin and suggest otherwise. Grub considered the whole event a great success and celebrated by firing Momma into the sky until another explosive sneeze finally rendered him unconscious.

lore: Like any decent Gnoll, Bok Singefur grew up in the Wild Plains, and was involved in at least three separate incendiary incidents before adulthood. He survived entirely by accident, mostly because the Gnoll Gods seem determined to keep their worshippers from going extinct. By the time he reached maturity he was already known as the craziest Gnoll in the kingdom, which is quite an achievement.

Bok plays with explosives in ways that make Goblins look cautious and responsible. He doesn’t just throw bombs, he sniffs them, tastes them, and runs his fingers through the black powder like it is fine sand on a beach. He has lost so much fur and skin to his hobby that he has had to rivet metal plates directly onto himself, a process he cheerfully calls ‘plating up’.

A Tauros Chief once asked Bok why he was called Singefur, and he simply tapped one of his riveted plates and said ‘metal better than fur’. He demonstrated this philosophy by lighting three bombs at once, laughing as they went off around him, then riveting a new plate over a burnt patch. The Tauros now insist he announce his arrival before entering their camps, mostly so they have time to hide anything flammable.

lore: Manasa grew up in the deep swamps of the Mist of Scales, where most Naga Queens are fearsome, regal, and very clear about who is allowed to approach them. She grew into a giant blue naga with unusual markings and a face that looked strangely human whenever she closed her mouth. Many creatures found that face comforting, right up until the moment they went into it.

Manasa can use her pleasant visage to lure in anyone foolish enough to trust a pair of luscious purple lips in the middle of a swamp. She can charm diplomats, merchants, and wandering heroes with equal ease, all while deciding whether they would make better allies or appetisers. She is considered perfect for delicate negotiations, provided no one minds the occasional disappearance.

Manasa’s skills might best be described as ‘gastronomic diplomacy’. In the Forest of Thorns she returned with a peace agreement and a dozen elves for snacks, which she claimed was a cultural misunderstanding. In Grosh-Nak she married an Orcish warlord, used his tribe to strengthen her homeland’s borders, and then ate him and his entire family on the journey home, which the Mist of Scales considered a very successful mission.

lore: The Faceless Lord was once Gancanagh of the Dark Court, a child cursed to be the most beautiful creature alive, which turned out to be far more inconvenient than it sounds. Nobody ever listened to a word he said, because they were too busy swooning, sighing, or fainting dramatically. Tired of being admired instead of heard, he donned a mask and left the Underworld behind.

But Gancanagh’s mind was sharp, and it finally received the attention it deserved once he reached Krystara. The Fey of Mydnight knew nothing of his curse, so they judged him by his leadership and cleverness rather than his unfairly perfect face. They called him the Faceless Lord, and he never corrected them, just in case someone connected the dots.

Soon after he arrived, Mydnight itself fell under a curse, which only confirmed his suspicion that curses follow him like lost puppies. Despite this, he helped Feyr organize the kingdom and became one of its most respected figures. To this day nobody has seen beneath the mask, and he intends to keep it that way, because the last thing he needs is another crowd fainting at his feet.

lore: Ser Gladis of Whitehelm earned the title of Soul Knight long before she ever became Undead, thanks to her love of gospel, rhythm and blues, and anything that involved a good beat. She founded her own lively church where hymns were accompanied by swords slamming against shields, which startled visiting clergy but delighted the troops. Her voice could lift spirits, shake rafters, and occasionally crack a helmet or two.

Ser Gladis was always able to blend music with battle, turning marches into melodies and skirmishes into full concerts. Even in armor she could sway, stomp, and sing with perfect rhythm, inspiring her soldiers to fight harder and louder. She believed that a good hymn could banish fear, and a great one could make even the staunchest Bishop tap their foot.

Sadly - like so many knights - Ser Gladis fell in battle against the Necromancers of Khetar and was raised as an Undead servant. Instead of obeying though, she broke free with the sheer force of song, belting out a hymn so powerful it sent the necromancers running for their un-lives. Now she patrols the borders of Khetar as an Undead knight, still singing, still fighting, and still keeping perfect time.

lore: NAV-1057 was one of the earliest navigation mechs built in Adana, created long before engineers realised that directions should ideally lead somewhere useful. Designed by the Master Engineer Tesla as a prototype for the far more reliable NAV-345Y, these mechs were shipped all over the kingdom with cheerful confidence. They quickly became famous for getting travelers to their destinations about sixty three percent of the time, which was considered excellent by early Adanian standards.

NAV-1057 units are quite personable, and good for a chat on a long journey, which unfortunately is not the same thing as ‘accurate navigation’. They love collecting old maps, even the wildly outdated ones that show kingdoms that no longer exist and rivers that never did. Their propensity for reading these may in part explain their inability to end up in the right place thirty seven percent of the time.

Because of their inaccuracy, many enthusiasts keep NAV-1057s in groups of three and follow whichever two agree on a route, a system that works beautifully until all three disagree and must be rebooted before it comes to mechanical fisticuffs. This also practically eliminates their inherent one percent chance of picking a route that leads to a fiery death. Tesla has never told anyone, but this grouping of 3 NAV-1057s is actually the core design of the NAV-345Y.

lore: Rhona Bittershield was born in the gloomy tunnels of Dhrak Zum long ago, where even the lanterns seem unhappy. She disliked everyone from an early age, including her family, her neighbours, and anyone who suggested she smile. Her greatest childhood sorrow was being denied a shield, which set the tone for a lifetime of bitterness, and also the tone of the name she took.

Rhona uses this bitterness to channel pure, unfiltered rage, which has only intensified after being killed by the Ice Daemon Glaycion and returned as a ghost. She never wanted a great axe, yet she is now cursed to wield it forever, which has not improved her mood. As a spirit she drifts through the abandoned halls, glowering at anything foolish enough to move, breathe, or even worse… move AND breathe.

Rhona does make a formidable guardian and steward of Dhrak-Zum though. She once saw a Dragon poke its snout into her halls, disturbing her miserable brooding. She erupted in a storm of spectral fury and chased it as far as Stormhaim’s border, like a startled bat. Even the gods tend to leave her alone now, because nothing is more dangerous than a Dwarf who has been denied a shield for two lifetimes.

lore: Dwarves did not always have mine carts, which is surprising given how much they love digging. In the early days they hauled every lump of ore out on their backs, which some say is why the entire race ended up frumpy, stumpy, and permanently grumpy. It was honest work, but it did nothing for their posture.

Things changed when one bright Dwarf suggested using Mimics to carry the ore, since Mimics already looked like chests and were always hungry. This worked well enough as long as the Mimics were fed, though every so often one would forget its job and remember it had teeth. Productivity soared, but so did the number of missing limbs.

The plan fell apart when the Mimics unionised and demanded an unreasonable number of Goblins as snacks before every shift. Luckily this happened just as the Dwarves discovered a strange round thing called a wheel, which they immediately attached to a box. Thus the first Mine Cart was born, and the Mimics were politely shown the exit before they could negotiate dental benefits.

lore: Born in the icy halls of the Winter Court, Fionnuala’s parents expected her to study ancient lore and NOT twirl through moonlit snowdrifts. They insisted she focus on books, scrolls, and more books, which only encouraged her to sneak out at night to dance with friends beneath the shimmering auroras. When they finally caught her, they packed her off to Silverglade to study under the High Elven scholar Tassarion, who managed to turn her into a brilliant academic, at least for a while.

Unfortunately one night, after drinking an unwise amount of Silverglade’s Honeywine, she danced straight into the lair of the Dragon Krystenax and taught the royal dragons a rather saucy Fey jig. The dragons loved it, the royal family did not, and she was promptly banished back to the Glacial Peaks. She lives there still, a scholar of great renown who has absolutely no regrets about introducing dragons to nightlife.

These days, Fionnuala weaves magic and knowledge together with the same grace she once used in her secret dances. She can recite ancient runes, unravel complex enchantments, and still find time to practice a few steps when no one is looking. She is a respected sage now, though she keeps her hair loose and her feet ready, just in case music happens. And occasionally she encourages it to happen… rather vigorously.

lore: Erendriel Darkweave was born in the shadowed forests of Zhul Kari, where spiders are involved in everything from politics to public transport. This was deeply unfortunate for her, because she loathed spiders with every fiber of her being, from the tiny temple communion spiders to the giant twenty seater bus spiders. Leaving the kingdom was unthinkable though, because she loved the forest itself - at least the non-spidery bits.

Erendriel is a mage, and she originally chose this career path as a way to avoid touching anything with more than four legs. Erendriel can conjure wards, illusions, and blasts of arcane force, all while keeping a very safe distance from anything even slightly spidery. She absolutely refuses to enter the spider temple - but will happily leave any small arachnid alone if it is 100’ away - which she considers a fair religious compromise.

Given her severe arachnophobia, it is not surprising she has turned much of her energy to working against the spider queens and spider priestesses who rule Zhul’Kari. She once led an anti-establishment uprising that replaced a sacred spider statue with a carved wooden badger. Today, she works with various rebellious factions throughout the kingdom, fighting for a future with fewer legs and far less mandatory spider-eating.

lore: Ciaran the Centaur was born in the rolling green plains of the Divinion Fields, where most centaurs spend their nights stargazing and their days galloping heroically towards the horizon. He wasn’t much of a galloper, so he chose a different path, deciding that travel was far more enjoyable when someone else did the hard work. By the time he reached adulthood he had already perfected the art of securing the most luxurious seat on any vehicle that would tolerate him.

Ciaran calls himself a ‘travel influencer’, though no one in Krystara is entirely sure what that means (including Ciaran). He simply flashes his perfect smile, flicks his magnificent hair, and somehow ends up with front row dragon seating or a royal suite on a Merlantis cruise. He can also dance on command, which he insists is essential to his brand, though no one has figured out why.

Ciaran calls his little enterprise ‘@travelswithciazza’ though the pronunciation of the first letter stumps most good folk. What also confuses people is that during the Grand Tour of Krystara, he reviewed every major kingdom while never once walking between them. But his glowing reports have inspired countless others to travel. To this day he trots from luxury to luxury, quill in hoof, documenting the world one pampered adventure at a time.

lore: The Webbed Prince began life as a rather bookish Dark Elf in Zhul’Kari, a kingdom where queens and priestesses usually run everything and princes are mostly decorative. His fate changed the day a magical spider bit him, giving him the ability to leap, cling to walls, and shoot webs from his hands. Overnight he transformed from a quiet nerd into a prankster of legendary proportions.

The Webbed Prince considers mischief a noble calling. He swings through palace halls, drops from ceilings, and ties up unsuspecting nobles in sticky webs, all while proudly declaring his motto: With Great Power Comes Great Irresponsibility. The priestesses tried to discipline him, but it was hard to punish someone who can simply climb out of anywhere you put them.

As he grew older, simple pranks no longer satisfied him though, and he discovered that other Dark Elves would actually follow his lead. This inspired him to attempt the greatest prank in history, which he described as conquering the world for a laugh. He now marches across the realms with a cackling grin, convinced that global domination will be the funniest joke anyone has ever attempted.

lore: Seditius began his rise to power in the ancient city of Hellcrag long before its people were cursed into stone, and even then nobody liked him very much. He clawed his way up the ranks of the military by removing anyone who stood between him and a promotion, usually by pushing them off cliffs when no one was looking. By the time he became a general, the entire city knew exactly how he had earned the title and avoided him with great enthusiasm.

He is an opportunistic assassin, which he considers a refined strategic art despite never once planning anything more complex than a shove or a poisoned tart. Seditius is not the strongest warrior, nor the smartest, but he is very good at being in the right place at the wrong time for someone else. To him, every person is a potential threat, rival, or stepping stone, and he treats them accordingly

He once eliminated three political rivals in a single afternoon by pretending to admire the view from a very tall balcony. Everyone knew he had done it, and he knew they knew, but no one dared speak up unless they wanted a midnight rendezvous with an arsenic-laced croissant. When the curse struck and turned the city to stone, Seditius became a red winged stone daemon, which he considered a promotion, as it made it easier to get to places where the pushing was done.

lore: In the shimmering halls of Merlantis, where Merfolk learn to swim before they learn to speak, young Balearic rose quickly through the ranks of the royal guard. Clad in armor forged from leviathan scales and wielding a trident carved from royal coral, by the time he became a knight, he cut a noble figure indeed. Unfortunately he fretted about absolutely everything.

Balearic can command the tides, a talent that makes him a formidable defender of Merlantis and a complete menace to anyone trying to fish peacefully. He can summon waves, whirlpools, and currents with a flick of his trident, usually because he has mistaken a harmless visitor for an invading armada. His seriousness is legendary - he once mistook a flock of seagulls for a flight of dragons, and had all Merlantis shelter in place for a week.

Sadly, Balearic’s most memorable moment is known as the Great Shell Scare, when he discovered a new type of seashell and declared that the Gods had birthed new monsters to destroy the world. He spent a month rallying the entire guard, only for it to turn out to be an ordinary shell. Despite the embarrassment, the Merfolk keep him around, because when a real danger finally appears, Balearic is the one knight who will already be in full armor, shouting orders, and ready to save the day.

lore: Tox and Sion were born in the volcanic kingdom of Broken Spire, where Two-Headed Ettin parents consider dangling their children over toxic pools a wholesome family activity. During one such game, when a juicy Rhynax walked past, their distracted father dropped them, and while they climbed out unharmed, the incident left them… changed. They blame the toxic cloud surrounding them on this incident, though it may also be due to a lifelong commitment to eating falafels.

Tox and Sion each control half of their body which makes walking difficult if they disagree on the destination. Arms are less impactful though. Sion controls one arm and spends every waking moment trying to make it stronger so he can hit things harder. Tox controls the other arm and has learned just enough magic to make everything more poisonous, which he considers a refined art despite all evidence to the contrary.

Tox’s head was born a minute earlier so he insists he is the leader. To be fair, he is the smarter of the two, though being smarter than Sion is not exactly a towering achievement. The truth is they work well together - Tox creates problems by thinking he is clever, and Sion solves them by knowing he is not. Their continued dedication to gaining victories over self-created issues has cemented their reputation as unstoppable agents of chaos.

lore: Ranger Evgeniy grew up in Urskaya, where the bear folk grow up learning to survive blizzards, avalanches, and the occasional grumpy mammoth. Even among the Urska he stood out as a no-nonsense brute who believed that hesitation was just a slower way of saying failure. By the time he reached adulthood he had already earned a reputation for reaching destinations faster than anyone else, mostly because nothing that stood in his way stayed standing for long.

If a single phrase could sum up Evgeniy it would be ‘forward momentum’, both physical and philosophical. Evgeniy does not negotiate, bargain, or pause to consider alternatives, because alternatives are for people who enjoy thinking. If he wants something, he takes it, and if something tries to stop him, he removes it with the efficiency of a snowplow powered by pure stubbornness.

Once, when crossing Frostbite Pass, an entire Wargare warband tried to block his route through the mountains. Evgeniy simply walked through them, flattening the warband, their barricade, and a small section of icy cliff before continuing on his way without comment. To this day the Urska say that if Evgeniy is headed somewhere, the smartest thing you can do is choose a different destination.

lore: Velosia hails from Vulpacea, where agility is prized, cleverness is expected, and stealing unattended chickens is considered a cultural tradition. From a young age she trained in Warg Jutsu, the Vulpacean paw-to-paw martial art that turns nimble foxfolk into whirling blurs of fur and death. By adulthood she could outfight warriors twice her size and look stylish while doing it.

Over the years, Velosia learned how to take on foes ten times her size. She can leap from limb to limb on an opponent like an acrobatic squirrel with the zoomies, striking pressure points with unerring accuracy. She darts from shoulder to elbow to knee in a heartbeat, leaving her foes bruised, confused, feeling rather used. When she finally hops off and taps them lightly, they collapse in a heap, usually apologizing for getting in her way.

Underneath the extremely lethal and competent exterior, she is still a fox though. In more than one life-or-death battle, she has lost all composure when spotting a plump chicken strutting nearby. The other Vulpacean fox folk may praise her heroism, but they still keep their hens locked up whenever she visits.

lore: Cycads were once peaceful gardeners in the elemental kingdom of Nexus, where they coaxed flowers into blooming brighter than the sun. They were gentle creatures who loved tending petals and pruning vines, but they had one weakness - gambling. They would gamble on absolutely anything, from how many petals were on a rose, to how many inches of rain would fall tomorrow, or how many acorns you can fit into a squirrel.

Then, one day, Mother Malice came to Nexus. She immediately saw this weakness and, hatching a cunning plan that for once all three heads agreed on, she introduced them to poker, blackjack, and pai-gow. Cycads may love gambling, but they sure are bad at it. Half the Cycads lost everything before they even learned the rules.

By the time Mother Malice left, those Cycads who had lost everything fell apart, becoming corrupted. They turned to shady dealings and dubious substances, selling their fronds on the green market for just… one… more… hit… And the once perfect gardens of Nexus? They were left looking like someone forgot which end of the rake to hold.

lore: Sir Geoffrey began his life in the orderly kingdom of Swords Edge, where knights were expected to be noble, disciplined, and at least moderately coordinated. Miraculously, he made it into the Knights Coronet thanks to his handsome hair and regal profile, which distracted everyone from the fact that he tripped over his scabbard twice during the induction ceremony. Still, he always tried his best, even if his best was usually followed by an apology and a loud splash.

Sadly, Sir Geoffrey’s moniker - The Fallen - came not from a heroic death in glorious battle, but the fact that he slipped off a ledge and plunged plume-first into a pool of toxic liquid. It was the very first meeting of the Knights Coronet and the Shadow Dragon, which involved a dangerous trek along a narrow ledge - something Sir Geoffrey was ill-equipped for. One predictable stumble later… off the ledge he went.

Sir Geoffrey the Fallen’s untimely death did at least spare him having to endure the corruption and disbanding of the Knights Coronet. The dark magic of the Shadow Dragon’s lair DID however resurrect him as an undead servant, but he was so bad at following orders that the Shadow Dragon eventually threw him out. This left him to wander Swords Edge forever as the clumsiest, most apologetic Undead knight in history.

lore: Blonk, the perfectly ordinary Hill Giant, was born in Stormheim. Like all his people, he was large, large, loud, and fond of snacks. His mama told him he could grow up to be anything he wanted, so he decided he would become a Storm Giant. From that day on Blonk trained with great enthusiasm and very little understanding of the impossibility of his ambition. He was, however, treading the path to becoming the famed Storm Oracle.

Blonk, you see, is an unfailing optimist, which he applies to everything from exercise to electrocution. After many failed attempts to wield lightning, he finally managed to shock himself so thoroughly that he danced around babbling nonsense. He immediately declared this to be prophecy, and since nobody could prove otherwise, Blonk simply decided he was the Storm Oracle. Everyone laughed at him.

Not to be deterred, Blonk sought out Jotnar Stormshield, the most electrifying Storm Giant in all of Stormheim. Upon enthusiastically grabbing Jotnar’s leg, Blonk’s cry for attention quickly turned into a high voltage stream of gibberish. Jotnar seemed to discern something deep and primal in Blonk’s painful shrieking - he decided this was clearly prophecy at work, and declared Blonk the Storm Oracle on the spot. Nobody ever argues with Jotnar.

lore: Shar'Gral grew up in a rough Orc clan where most children collected scars, but she collected wolves instead. Her first pup, Warfang, became her closest companion, and from that moment she simply never stopped adding more to the pack. By adulthood she had so many wolves that the clan elders stopped asking where she found them and started asking where she planned to put them.

While many know Shar’Gral as the ‘Crazy Wolf Lady’, she really is just a wolf wrangler extraordinaire. Shar'Gral can calm a snarling beast with a hug, steal a wolf from under another rider, and even convince the grumpiest mother wolf to hand over her pups. Warfang remains her favourite though, carrying her into battle with the weary patience of someone who has seen far too many siblings arrive uninvited.

Shar’Gral’s pack has grown at such a rate that she has had to move huts no less than seven times. The last time is referred to as the Siege of Bonecrack Hold, when she arrived at her new home with so many wolves that they swarmed the nearby battlements, terrifying the guards. Shar’Gral hopes this empty keep will be big enough, though after the infamous roof-eating incident she fears she’ll need to get back into the market shortly.

lore: No Hag ever starts her miserable existence as a Twisted Hag. They all begin brewing foul potions for Darkstone’s tyrants, a job that involves far too many fumes and far too little safety. Every so often one slips, stumbles, or is given a helpful shove into her own cauldron, and what emerges is something far more warped than before. Even other Hags - not known for their high standards - tend to cross the street when they see one coming.

Twisted Hags serve a vital role in the Darkstone ecosystem; they create the potions so mind-alteringly dangerous that even the Darkstone Lords read the labels twice, which is saying something for people whose idea of a nutritious breakfast is a pill, a potion, and a perfectly-juiced kitten. The ability to create the ‘good stuff’ though is very useful - in the same way that sticks of dynamite are useful when you need a door opened quickly.

One infamous Twisted Hag, known only as Grindle, once brewed a potion that made an entire battalion of slavemasters actually kind for a week. The resultant outbreak of liberty and rebellion almost toppled the monarchy who were so horrified that they have tolerated Twisted Hags with great reluctance ever since, provided they stand very still and do not stir anything without warning.

lore: Mother Malice began life as a Fey child of the Dark Court, bright and curious until Daemons dragged her through the portal of the Sin of Maraj. They imprisoned her for millenia, forcing her to brew horrific potions until one experiment sprouted a second head, and a later argument between the two resulted in a third. By the time she escaped to Krystara, she had three bickering voices and a very firm idea of how children should be put to work.

Thousands of years of aggressive dabbling has made her able to brew the most horrific concoctions, so much so that even Daemons learned to keep a safe distance. Each head has its own specialty, which would be impressive if they ever agreed on anything for more than a heartbeat. Still, their combined skill is unmatched, provided you don’t mind the occasional explosion or spontaneous transformation.

After her dramatic escape though, Mother Malice founded the Darkstone Hags, a coven created by kidnapping children and teaching them the same dreadful arts she had endured. For a time she ruled them with all three heads shouting orders, until the Hags finally unionized and sealed her in a pocket dimension for the sake of workplace harmony. Rumor has it she is still in there, arguing with herself and planning a dramatic return.

lore: Lapina are typically burrow dwellers, digging tunnels so vast that they accidentally connected half of Krystara to the Underworld. But every so often a particularly adventurous Lapina looks out to sea, decides it is just a very large puddle, and sets off to steal anything not nailed down. It happens often enough that there are whole ships of them, armed with charm, mischief, and an alarming number of grappling hooks.

They weave trickery and allure into a single irresistible package. A Lapina Pirate can smile sweetly while cutting your purse strings, then whisper words so enchanting that you thank them for the experience. When sailors see their black flag - the skull and cross-bunnies - on the horizon, half the crew swoon and the other half hide the silverware.

Life at sea can be pretty dull and boring, so it’s not unheard of for some ships to simply drop anchor, and just invite the Lapina Pirates to simply hop aboard. They can then enjoy some outrageous flirtation and a little risqué dancing, in exchange for whatever is lying around in the hold - that’s what insurance is for, isn’t it? All things considered, it’s a far more civilized and enjoyable form of piracy.

lore: Grave Worms are usually seen in ancient battlefields and graveyards where the body-to-soil ratio is quite high. These colossal worms slither up from the depths, not for the bodies themselves but for the delicious bones inside. To them, a well stocked ossuary or catacomb is less a place of mourning and more an all-you-can-eat buffet.

They extract calcium with the enthusiasm of a creature that has discovered its one true purpose. A Grave Worm can strip a skeleton clean in seconds, grind the bones to powder, and then roll in the dust like a happy, enormous cat in a mountain of catnip. This habit also makes them a menace to dairies, as they will gleefully dive into milk vats in search of that same calcium kick.

One legendary Grave Worm, known as Old Cruncher, once destroyed an entire cellar of Brie during the Great Cheese Festival of Highmoor. The townsfolk still talk about the chaos that followed, as the worm rampaged through the streets in a euphoric haze, like a cheese platter on a 3-day bender. It finally burrowed away, leaving behind a trail of empty rinds and several traumatised cheesemakers who have never trusted a cellar floor since.

lore: Hollioke lives in the southern reaches of the Bright Forest, where the Summer Court keeps its most troublesome Fey safely distracted with festivals and fruit wine. From the start she showed all the charm of a thorny rose, lovely to look at but best admired from a distance. Parents across the realm still warn their children that if they hear giggling in the bushes, it might be Hollioke and they should run.

She stirs chaos with the grace of a seasoned chef, usually while pretending she had nothing to do with it. She can twist a simple greeting into a mortal insult with a flick of her fingers, then sit back and enjoy the resulting argument. Other Fey swear she must have a cat somewhere in her ancestry, because, well… show else could she look so self-satisfied?

Once, during the Summer Moonlight Revel, she lured a group of mortals straight into a Fey gathering just to see what would happen. When the expected chaos failed to erupt, she helpfully cast a few spells to convince the mortals that the Fey were actually hungry pink dragons, and to convince the Fey that the mortals were rampaging purple Ogres. The resulting scuffle is still talked about today, mostly by people who insist they were definitely winning.

lore: Gindibu rose to fame in the Leonis Empire as a fearsome warrior. Although most people assumed his brilliance came from long hours of training, in truth he simply climbed onto his camel one day, waved a spear about, and everyone decided he looked heroic enough. The camel, affectionately called Humps, had far more brains than his rider, and accepted this arrangement with an un-camel-like amount of grace.

Gindibu does have one paramount skill though - remaining seated while Humps does all the thinking. The camel signals battle plans with well timed spits, grunts, and the occasional pointed glare, which Gindibu interprets as divine guidance. Together they form a surprisingly effective duo, provided no one asks Gindibu to explain what’s going on.

Once, when surrounded by an enemy battalion, Humps managed to mimic being stuck in quicksand. As the enemies fell about laughing at them, one well-placed spit-and-charge, followed by some enthusiastic spear-waving, found the enemy commander lying in three pieces and the enemies in retreat. To this day, the Leonis Empire celebrates them both, though only one of them understands why.

lore: Like most Vulture-Stryx, Cinereous was hatched in a quiet Suncrest rookery where he would learn the gentle art of tending the dead. He took to this with enthusiasm, though his elders often wished he would stop smiling quite so much during funerals. By the time he reached adulthood, he had become a respected figure in the cult of Zilopochtli, at least by those who did not know him well.

Cinereous claims he can sense when someone is nearing their final breath, which he treats as an invitation rather than a warning. While other Vulture Stryx wait patiently for nature to take its course, Cinereous prefers to give fate a helpful nudge with a well placed blade. He insists this is a sacred duty, though the fact that he only nudges wealthy targets has raised a few feathers.

Cinereous once performed what he calls his finest service when he singlehandedly performed the last rites on an entire corrupt merchant council. The cult of Zilopochtli praised the act as a grand purification, though they did wonder why he kept all the council’s jewelry. Cinereous simply bowed, claimed it was an offering to Zilopochtli, and strutted off to find his next worthy contribution.

lore: Merneith joined the necromantic priesthood of the Anubites with great enthusiasm but absolutely no talent for raising the dead. Every spell she attempted resulted in nothing more than a polite rattling cough from a nearby skeleton. The elders eventually gave her a dangerous-looking Khopesh-on-a-stick, and decided she was better suited to tasks that did not involve animation.

What Merneith lacked in necromantic skill though, she made up for with an uncanny knack for feeding the undead. She discovered that mummies, when given regular meals of scarab pasta and Gnome stew (the kind made FROM Gnomes, not BY them), became surprisingly well behaved. Before long she had created an entire department dedicated to keeping the tombs quiet, tidy, and blissfully un-rampaged.

During the Great Tomb Stirring, when a sandstorm rattled half the sarcophagi in Khetar and threatened a full scale mummy uprising, Merneith arrived with a wagon of fresh Gnomes and soothed the entire horde with the efficiency of someone feeding very cranky housecats. The kingdom was saved, the mummies settled back into their wrappings, and Merneith was promoted to Head of Eternal Hospitality.

lore: Sanguinette began life as a perfectly ordinary guardsman in Hellcrag, at least as ordinary as anyone can be in a city that regularly dabbled in curses. When the great curse fell, he turned to stone on the spot, which was inconvenient for him but extremely convenient for the thief he had been chasing. Over the next thousand years he slowly regained movement, mostly to glare at trespassers.

His unusual talent is that he grows a little larger every time he defeats an intruder, which is excellent for intimidation and terrible for moving through doorways. By the time he reached fifty feet tall, most travelers decided that whatever was inside Hellcrag was not worth the risk. Sanguinette himself never commented, but his habit of looming suggested he approved.

After the curse was lifted, a group of bold Hellcragians discovered that he could be picked up and carried like a very angry siege engine. They set him down beside enemy walls, where he happily smashed fortifications with the enthusiasm of someone making up for a millennium of boredom. No one knows if he enjoys his work, but given the way he pulverizes anything he is pointed at, he certainly seems content enough.

lore: Blood Spores start their life as small pimples on the landscape. Unlike ordinary blemishes, they are filled with a sticky, blood-like goo that smells faintly of strawberries and doom. They are eldritch in origin, and likely 100% vegan, though eating them has proved to be a very bad idea, even if scones and clotted cream are involved.

A Blood Spore’s most unsettling talent is luring prey with that sweet aroma, which wafts across the shattered lands of Karakoth like a sinister bakery. Once a creature wanders close, the Blood Spore bursts open, sprouting tendrils and teeth that grab anything foolish enough to have a sniff. The larger they grow, the hungrier they become, and the less picky about what counts as dinner.

The most famous battle involving Blood Spores actually didn’t involve a Blood Spore at all. It occurred when Cedric Sparklesack, leading a contingent of Soul Gnomes, smothered themselves in strawberry jam and snuck into a Warlock’s Tower to steal his secret Soul Cache. Smelling berries, and fearing for his life, the Warlock fled. Cedric’s Sack was stuffed full that day, but it did coin the phrase: ‘Never trust a sticky Gnome’.

lore: Young Aqen Bloodclaw was nothing but trouble. From his earliest days, he styled himself as a tragic hero, complete with swooshing cloak and dramatic pauses. His neighbors quickly learned that any performance ended with missing jewelry.

His greatest skill is turning ordinary moments into theatrical productions, complete with ominous lighting and suspicious exits. Aqen can vanish in a swirl of fabric, only to reappear behind you holding your purse. He claims this is ‘art’, though most of his victims would think of it more as ‘robbery with 5 extra steps’.

For this reason, Aqen was exiled. Repeatedly. First from every town in the Pridelands, and then from the Pridelands itself. More than one monarch has tried to exile him from Krystara itself, but nobody is quite sure how that works, or how to enforce it. It does mean he’s become quite proficient at traveling though, and in many circles he is known as the ‘Most Unreliable Guide in Krystara’.

lore: Like most Goblins, Lord Gobthe came from nothing. But from a young age he was so filled with bravado and self-confidence, that it was clear he was going somewhere, even if that place was just an early grave. He was unbearable - even for a Goblin - so much so that at 8 years old, after demanding his parents bow down before him, and address him as Lord Gobthe, his mother strangled him in his sleep and threw him in a river.

It seems his self-belief was strong enough to bring him back to life (though it may just have been his mother’s weak arthritic grip). Either way, after his miraculous rebirth, he returned the favor to both his parents, then took an interest in necromancy so he could raise them from the dead to FINALLY call him Lord Gobthe, which they continue to this day with a series of moans and eye-rolling.

Using his necromantic powers less for grand armies and more for personal validation, he then added the skeletons of a few aunts and uncles to his entourage who clap politely when he enters a room. It would be unwise to underestimate Gobthe though… Anyone who laughs at him is strangled by his parents with surprising enthusiasm - it seems that zombification may be the ultimate cure for arthritis.

lore: Vinepyres trace their origins back to an overeager Wood Elf who tried to plant a rose bush on cursed soil and forgot to read the fine print. What grew instead was a hungry tangle of vines with a taste for Elf flesh and a complete disregard for gardening etiquette. Over time, the Forest of Thorns has become littered with these leafy predators, much to the dismay of the locals.

A Vinepyre’s greatest skill is patience, which is impressive for a plant that spends most of its life hungry. It can coil silently around trees, waiting for an Elf to wander too close, then strike with surprising speed and questionable table manners. Unfortunately, Elves may be tasty, but they are also kind of stringy without much meat on the bone, so Vinpyres augment their diets with an occasional distracted owlbear.

Vinepyres never stop growing. The largest one on record grew so large it blocked the entire southern gate of the City of Enthaven by picking off unwary travelers. It did once prove itself useful when it devoured a gaggle of attacking goblins, but sadly, the resulting burp was just too much for it, and it promptly collapsed, leaving behind a new generation of hungry seedlings.

lore: Queen Wilhelmina began her reign beside King Ghuldor, the King in Crimson. When Draakulis cursed her husband, and the King began sprouting wings and squeaking at odd hours, she decided marriage had its limits. She fled north, trading royal banquets for drafty halls and the company of one Lord Harker.

Queen Wilhemina’s own curse revealed itself slowly, first as an aversion to garlic soup and later as a fondness for moonlight. And fresh blood. Unlike most vampires, she retained her regal poise and a talent for turning polite conversation into hypnotic suggestion. Sadly, she also passed the curse to Lord Harker, who found all this rather charming until he realized he was agreeing to redecorate the castle in the blood of his subjects.

Together they became infamous across Ghulvania, ruling their northern keep with elegance and only an occasional bit of biting. It turns out that even small amounts of biting can get on the nerves of the peasantry though, and eventually the peasants revolted, sealing the pair away… though legends say Wilhelmina still lives deep in her tomb.

lore: A Wulf Gheist is born when a Wargare is murdered while communing with the spirit realm. Their connection at the time allows them to refuse to stay politely dead. Instead, they reform as a restless and destructive spirit (is there any other kind?).

Their talent lies in mischief that escalates quickly from rattling doors to collapsing barns. A Wulf Gheist can howl so loudly that it shakes the bones of the living, and occasionally rearranges furniture in ways that defy both gravity and taste. Sages have speculated they may have been frustrated interior decorators in life, but if you’ve ever seen a messy Wargare hovel, feng shui is the last thing on their crooked little minds.

Wulf Gheists are invisible most of the time, but their glowing eyes will appear just long enough to make you nervous. After that, the balls of glowing red energy they command will appear just long enough to completely ruin your evening. And after that… well… you’re usually running screaming, so it’s not terribly important what happens next.

lore: Mor'Zarn is an Orc Shaman who was excommunicated from the Cult of Zorn and survived. Why was he thrown out? How did he survive? The answer is the same to both questions - by thinking for himself (a trait that is more rare amongst Orcs than flower arranging, artisanal baking, and landscape gardening… combined).

Shamans of Zorn only have two real jobs - the sacred arts of battle-boosting and post-battle bandaging. But Mor'Zarn invented protective totems that glowed faintly and made warriors slightly harder to stab. These totems were frowned upon by the elders, who believed pain was character-building and blood loss was motivational. Mor'Zarn disagreed, mostly because he was tired of mopping up motivational blood puddles.

The Tribal Elders were furious; mostly because this was not ‘the way things were done (tm)’, but also because they rather enjoyed sitting back with a skull-full of janga juice on a Monday night and watching a good bloodbath. They threw Mor’Zarn off a precipice known as the Screaming Cliff and called it a day. Fortunately for Mor’Zarn, his stash of protective totems saved him, and he now wanders Grosh-Nak handing out those totems to any Orcs smart enough to want one (spoiler: that's not very many of them).

lore: Amethony was hatched to two proud Black Dragonian parents in a cave full of stolen silverware and pilfered packages, which may explain his lifelong confusion about both the postal service and dinner etiquette. To everyone’s surprise, he was a rare purple Dragonian. His parents, both respectable rogues, were proud and slightly alarmed.

Purple Dragonians are just too glittery to sneak anywhere, and Amethony was doubly blessed with the glitter-gene. He sparkled so hard that he wouldn’t have been able to sneak past a blind mole on a foggy night. Fortunately, he had a fondness for guiding others - occasionally to their doom, and occasionally to an ambush - but hey, it was still a career niche.

During one ill-fated journey through the Forest of Thorns - of the kind Amethony is best known for - he led a group of merchants past three Elven ambushes, discovered a forgotten shrine, accidentally activated a blessing, and then saved the group from a cursed fog that smelled like old Elven cheese. The merchants later nominated Amethony for a medal, which mysteriously vanished before the ceremony along with half of their cargo.

lore: Ariosa was born beneath a weeping willow that sobbed melodically when it heard her first cries. The locals mostly took this as a good omen (though some thought it was a plumbing issue). Raised among the flute-playing satyrs and overly dramatic squirrels of Pan’s Vale, she learned to sing before she learned to walk.

Ariosa’s voice is a weapon disguised as a serenade, capable of turning even the grumpiest beast into a puddle of joy and then, quite suddenly, into confetti. This technique, known as ‘aggressive vocalization’, is banned in most taverns and politely ignored in diplomatic circles. Ariosa herself insists she’s just trying to spread happiness… just preferably in a non-splattered form.

Once, during an attack on Pan’s Vale by Khaziel, Ariosa sang a ballad so moving that the invading Dwarves dropped their axes, hugged each other, and exploded in a cloud of glitter and emotional closure. The defenders were stunned, grateful, and slightly sticky. Ariosa was offered a medal, which she declined in favor of some nice hair ribbons and a promise that no one would ever ask her to sing at weddings.

lore: The Abominable Trolls of Urskaya were once regular Trolls with a fondness for bellowing, bridge-sitting, and other normal troll things. One day, for reasons that still remain unclear (but may have involved a lost bet in a game of smashy-face), they decided to move to the highest mountains. Most of them promptly froze, which was unfortunate but also a lesson in poor planning. The survivors adapted by wearing their less fortunate cousins like winter coats and pretending it was a cultural tradition.

Over the centuries, the Abominable Trolls evolved thick white fur that camouflaged them perfectly against snowbanks and confused passing goats, which often ended in a goat-sized snack. Thus, they developed a talent for ambushes that involved very little movement and a lot of waiting. Their idea of hunting turned into standing still until something edible walked into them and apologized.

All of that is not to say they’ve made no positive contributions! During the Great Avalanche of Grumbling Bear Pass, an entire village was saved when a herd of Abominable Trolls blocked the falling snow with their bodies and a surprising amount of stubbornness. They didn’t mean to help, they were just standing-still-stalking a herd of tasty goats, and had fallen asleep. The villagers built a shrine in their honor, which the Trolls later mistook for a snack and partially ate.

lore: Siobhan was born in the Royal Crystal Caverns, where her parents’ lullabies echoed amongst the stalactites and were only occasionally interrupted by the snoring of Krystenax, the Royal Dragon. Her family tended those caverns, and by the time she could walk, Siobhan could identify all the gems there, and even knew exactly how to bribe a dragon whelp with candied geodes.

She always had an uncanny knack for understanding how crystals resonate with magical energy and how the Crystal Dragons of Silverglade respond to that; she once calmed a rampaging hatchling by humming in the frequency of moonstone. She’s not afraid of a bit of strategic glittering either, which confuses enemies and delights allies.

Siobhan’s defining moment came when the Undead rose from the Bay of Stars and started redecorating the Royal Palace with seaweed and despair, Siobhan led a squad of Crystal Dragon whelps straight into the fray. She tuned the palace’s crystal chandeliers to emit a harmonic pulse that disrupted necromantic spells, while encouraging some enthusiastic nibbling from the young dragons. The royal family was so impressed they gave her a medal, and a very large budget for dragon treats.

lore: Commodore Maryka’s parents were Captain and First Mate of the Screaming Haddock - a pirate ship with more parrots than discipline. While the crew practiced swordplay and drinking, Maryka quietly taught herself math, mostly from old, stolen, and rum-stained ledgers. By the time she was sixteen, she could calculate compound interest faster than most of the crew could draw a cutlass.

Maryka’s true weapon is, and always will be, a ledger. Her greatest battles are fought with gold and silver, while she’s breached more contracts than enemy hulls. They say she’s so sharp that she once managed to board and conquer a rival ship by exploiting its unpaid docking fees, and that she keeps her treasure sorted by weight, sparkle, and likelihood of being cursed.

Her only defeat was to the fleet of Sword’s Edge, where Maryka still managed to negotiate peace by offering Queen Ysabelle a deal - a crate of doubloons and her unique expertise for mercy and the position of Royal Privateer. The Queen was so impressed she made Maryka a Commodore, and even gave her a Royal Accountant’s seal, which Maryka promptly used to write off three barrels of rum as ‘strategic morale assets’.

lore: Hornbreaker was born during an epic thunderstorm that ruined most of his village, including a statue of the War God, Ketras the Bull. His parents took that as a sign he would be a great warrior! Unfortunately, upon giving him his first axe at age 5, he used it to carve a riddle into the wall of his family home.

Although trained in the Minotaur arts of stomping and shouting, Hornbreaker preferred riddles and logic traps. He once defeated a Gnollish bandit by asking ‘What weighs a ton, makes your food, and smells faintly of onions’? After answering ‘Your Mom’, the Gnoll surrendered, confused and hungry, and later opened a bakery (which was, ironically, the answer to the riddle).

Hornbreaker likes to spend his time traveling the Wild Plains, and learning new riddles; he hopes one day to create his very own maze. But sometimes battle is unavoidable. His greatest victory was against Chief Fourhorn the Cleaver, where after 3 hours of incessant riddling and one accidental pun, the Chief’s brain overheated and three of his horns fell off, finally vindicating the name that Hornbreaker received all those years ago.

lore: They say the night Eridana was born was the same night that the Great Horned Comet appeared over the Divinion Fields. If that wasn’t a sufficiently portentous omen - much to the midwife’s surprise, and her mother’s shock - Eridana had a horn; a sure sign that a slightly sketchy Unicorn had managed to insert itself into her bloodline at some point. More importantly though - it was the sign of a master Star Gazer.

The omens proved to be true. From a very young age, Eridana could read the stars like a Wood Elf reads a vegetarian menu (except without complaining about the prices). Eridana has said that she doesn’t so much read the stars as converse with them. When they’re feeling particularly chatty, she is up all night.

Her demeanor? Always positive. The only thing she hates is clouds. It means the stars can’t talk to her, and she has to just sit up all night playing boardgames with the Moon Moths. She is happiest out on the plains, by herself, with a clear sky, talking with the stars as her horn glows a soft shade of red.

lore: Long ago, when the Mist of Scales was little more than a small puddle with big ambitions, the first Cascabel slithered forth from the egg-pits of Takshaka. Already well-aware of her purpose, she hissed twice, sacrificed a marsh-squirrel who blinked at her threateningly, and dedicated this first victim to her god and father, Takshaka. The Cascabels have only grown more unhinged and terrifying in the millenia that followed.

When a sacrifice takes place, Cascabels possess the unsettling ability to spread ailments so twisted and obscure that nobody is even sure what the symptoms are. And the purpose of this? Nobody knows, but many believe it is simply in service to Takshaka, who apparently enjoys a bit of creative suffering and a well-organized ritual.

For example… When the Royal Adanian Cartographers once tried to map the Mist of Scales, the Cascabels responded with flair. After catching one and performing a rather touching sacrificial ceremony, the entire Cartographers’ Guild was cursed to violently sneeze every time anyone said ‘north’. Adana quietly redrew the borders and sent a couple of violently-sneezing cartographers to the Cascabels in a care package by way of apology.

lore: Azbeel was not so much born as he was ignited, which is fairly normal if you happen to live in The Blighted Lands. In his first year, he managed to accidentally set fire to his crib, three pieces of outdoor furniture, the Daemonic hovel next door, and a stray hellcat. His parents, if you could call two volcanic eruptions ‘parents’, were very proud.

As so many young Daemons do, he eventually joined a Daemonic host - in this case, under Lord Baphomet. His proudest moment came when he accidentally set fire to an Orcish city. His fellow Daemons cheered - very impressed. The city itself was less impressed, but then cities usually are.

These days, Azbeel is looking for new cities to add to his list of ‘accidental renovations’. He claims it’s a hobby; the large fiery whip he wields, and the long lines of refugees, say otherwise. What is indisputable though is that he’s very very good at what he does.

lore: Krag'Rax’s father wanted to name his firstborn son Axe-Axe Blood-Axe, in honor of the long line of axe-wielding murderers that had produced him. Fortunately his mother insisted on something less likely to get him punched before breakfast. Thus, Krag'Rax entered the world with a slightly less ridiculous name, and a destiny drenched in sharp edges.

Krag'Rax certainly didn't disappoint his paternal ancestors. While most Orcs were content swinging axes, Krag'Rax decided to make them, enchant them, and occasionally argue with them. He learned the secrets of magical metallurgy from a group of Dwarves who he discovered were extremely flammable, and consequently very bad at keeping secrets. His forge smelled of molten iron, scorched beard, and ambition.

His most famous creation was "The Axe of the Horde" - a weapon imbued with not just his own will, but the maniacal murderous intent of his entire bloodline. This weapon was so horrendously violent, that nobody could pick it up without being touched by Krag'Rax's unique form of madness - an appetizer of a half-dozen beheadings, followed by a week-long main course of random dismemberment, and capped off with a cheeky murder spree.

lore: In the golden spires of Suncrest, where feathers are fashion and gossip has wings, Mayahuel hatched in the quiet alcove of the Grand Aviary Library. Her parents were archivists, her nest lined with scrolls instead of straw. By age five, she had already corrected the kingdom’s official history twice - once over breakfast.

Having stared at prose since she was an owlette, Mayahuel’s memory is so precise that she can quote everything from the footnotes of obscure cookbooks to the Great Treaty of the Eclipse. She once won a debate by listing every contradictory sentence in her opponent’s autobiography, in chronological order. Her talent is admired, feared, and occasionally used to settle bets about ancient poultry law.

Her greatest moment came during the Siege of Suncrest Temple by Chief Stronghorn of the Wild Plains. The High Priest faltered while casting the Song of Dismissal. As others panicked, Mayahuel calmly recited the entire Song from memory, including the obscure third verse about fermented berries. The Song worked, the invaders were banished, and Mayahuel returned to her desk with a sigh, muttering something about overdue scrolls.

lore: There was once a Dwarf named Khormac; he was possibly the laziest Dwarf to ever live in Dhrak-Zûm. Like his family before him, he was supposed to be a miner, but he could never be bothered lifting a pick. His father eventually pushed him into guard duty, but he could never be bothered lifting an axe either. They called him Khormac the Listless.

It turns out that not carrying your axe into battle is a really bad idea. The Dhrak-Zûm military motto has always been: ‘Strike first, Strike last’, so if you don’t have your axe, then the only thing you’ll be striking is THEIR axe, with YOUR face. To nobody’s surprise, that sums up exactly what happened in Khormac’s very first battle.

Khormac was SO lazy though, he couldn’t even be bothered passing into the afterlife. So his spirit remained, floating through the deep halls of Dhrak-Zûm, looking for a good place to rest - not an easy task in a frozen Daemon-infested hellscape - which has led to his new name, Khormac the Restless.

lore: Denwen was originally from the Pridelands, but he was always been a bit of a… well… wanderer. He started roaming the plains of his homeland when he was just a cub. Other Raksha told him that if he didn’t stop wandering, he’d wear his legs down and look like one of those useless city-cats with the short legs. But did Denwen listen? Not a chance.

As a Juvenile - looking for new places to wander - Denwen headed for the Leonis Empire. He was too restless to become a Prideguard, but he did manage to land work guarding caravans. This earned him some coin, while allowing him to keep wandering. The trouble with caravans is that they know where they’re going. Denwen kind of liked NOT knowing that - it’s what wandering was all about after all.

One day, leaving his caravan to be devoured by a Great Maw, he wandered off aimlessly into the Drifting Sands. The great thing about this place, he discovered, was that you NEVER knew where you were going, even when you had a destination in mind. And, to this day, Denwen can still be found there… wandering. And occasionally fighting something large and dangerous, which - it turned out - he was pretty great at too.

lore: The Spirit of Luck’s story is neverending. He is quite different to other Fey- they say he existed before Krystara, perhaps even before time itself - and that he will exist long after it has faded from memory… into nothing… He is distinctly Fae, yet fashioned from something more godlike.

Currently, like many spirits, he is drawn to the Kingdom of Vulpacea, where he can commune with the Spirit-Talkers. As is his custom, he has changed his shape somewhat to appear more fox-like. Here, due to his unusual talents he has quickly become a favorite spirit amongst the Vulpaceans.

His method of communication is unusual for a spirit. His ‘words’ appear as scripture in the air, which can be read, bestowing various boons and forms of good fortune upon those who read it. He can be found randomly floating through the forest - always carefree - and looking to distribute this luck to anyone whom he encounters.

lore: The Horusites are a small clan of creatures still persisting from the realm of Ancient Khet. They were far fewer in number than the Settites and Anubites, even though some may say their God was more important, being the God of the Sun. That said, their Champions are mighty, and play a part in modern Khetari power struggles.

In particular, the Horusites have a long-standing feud with the Settites, and it all relates to their respective Gods. Sett - the God of the Settites - killed the father of Horus - the God of the Horusites. This has never been, and will never be, forgiven, so the two factions are constantly at war.

The Anubites on the other hand are kindly disposed towards the Horusites, as their respective Gods were brothers. So the Horusites can always be counted on to take the side of the Anubites in any conflict. This is important, as having the power of one or more Horusite Champions on your side can turn the tide of a battle.

lore: Everyone has heard of the Iron Maiden - a horrific device shaped like a coffin, and filled with spikes to impale whoever is trapped inside. The Maiden of Pain is similar in idea, but much grander in its…ahh… execution. Only Daemonic minds could imagine such a thing, and this is indeed the invention of the Daemon Lord, Lust.

Rather than a single target, a whole host of unwilling creatures are fed in through two access points on the front of the Maiden of Pain. The maiden may then be opened to reveal the creatures impaled upon its giant spikes, and any Daemons in attendance may feast upon the souls it releases.

Because getting all those creatures to the Maiden of Pain is… ahh.. a pain, she has been fitted with wheels so she can be dragged around. Needless to say, the Daemons don’t do this themselves. It is an ‘honor’ reserved for the worst sinners. It is a dubious one, but the alternative - the very thing they drag around - is so much worse.

lore: Whitehelm has many Knightly Orders, and all manner of knights. It has been humorously observed that where Adana would build a contraption to solve a problem, Whitehelm would just create a new Knightly Order to do the same. Wasteful? Yes. Effective? Surprisingly so. If you give a group of people swords and armor, then put them on a performance-based contract, the results can be surprising.

While the Order of the Seeker has been around for centuries, it is unique in that it only ever has a single member. Other Knightly Orders tend to get bloated over time (as do their Knights, but that is a separate issue entirely). Some Orders even lose track of their original purpose. But the Order of the Seeker - with its single member - stays sharp, focused, and effective.

Ser Angelica is the current Seeker. She follows an esteemed line of previous Seekers who have all been powerful warriors, great leaders, and esteemed diplomats. But why is there only one Seeker, and what is their purpose? Simply put, the Seeker’s job is to make sure that the most important traveler in Whitehelm, at any point in time, gets to where they’re going safely.

lore: LOCK-1887, and its optional add-on WATTS-1927, are mechs created with the express purpose of solving difficult problems. Both have advanced optical, olfactory, and auditory scanners that can gather large quantities of information, with the main processing unit in LOCK-1887 correlating information and drawing conclusions.

They superseded the previous model from the College of Engineers, codenamed L-STRD-1924, which was well-known for only having a small amount of memory and producing spurious conclusions that were either misleading or downright incorrect.

Unfortunately, LOCK-1887 and WATTS-1927 tend to leave quite a mess as they work, so the College of Engineers has devised a further add-on, HDSN-221B, that is specifically programmed to follow them around and clean up their mess.

lore: Scrollweavers are not ordinary spiders - they are magical creatures, more alive than a construct such as a Golem, but spun from pure crystalline arcane energy in a way that leaves them not quite flesh and blood either. Their most distinctive feature is that they thrive on a diet of thought and knowledge.

Where a normal spider tries to trap its prey and devour it, the Scrollweaver will try to trap a creature and steal certain items. This includes scrolls and books - especially spellbooks. This limits their prey to spellcasters, which is why they’re predominantly found near Elven settlements, particularly in Zhul’Kari.

The origins of these strange creatures are unknown, though various sages have guessed they may once have been caretakers of an ancient and mystical library. Many expeditions have set out into the most Scollweaver-infested parts of the woods in search of the ruins of this library, but none have ever returned - perhaps a sign that it had other caretakers as well.

lore: The Sky Elves of Shentang have produced many notable warriors over the centuries, but perhaps none have mastered the art of aerial combat as well as Han Xin. Beginning his life as a Sky-Dancer, Han Xin blended the forms of traditional swordplay with the art of the dance to create something new, devastating, and deadly.

Up until Han Xin’s time, the traditional combat of the Sky Elves was more closely related to their pre-ascension forms; they would either fight from the ground, or simply use their wings to gain a brief aerial advantage as they attacked. Han Xin however believed these two things - fight and battle - should exist as equal parts of the martial form.

With that in mind, an upward sweep simply becomes part of launching in the air, while a downswing becomes part of a dive. Thrusting is often a forward somersault, while parries involve movement around, or even over, the target. Han Xin’s signature move - the Aerial Smite - involves a dive from 1000 feet in the air, where the smite actually forms part of an elegant landing.

lore: Mydnight is home to many creatures of many races. Having lived under the curse for so long, most of them have become Fey-touched, meaning they interact with Fey magic as part of their daily lives. So Mydnight is one of the few places in Krystara you might find a Fey-touched Dwarf!

The Fey-touched Dwarves of Mydnight - few though they are - have organized themselves into a Guild known as the Innovators. Here, their Dwarven natures take over, allowing them to craft all manner of wondrous machinery. What is unique about their inventions though, is that they are often powered by Fey magic.

Some of the creations of the Mydnight Innovators include self-polishing jewellery, a beer-stein that keeps refilling if you can balance on one leg for 10 seconds to prove you’re not drunk, a mining drill that alters directions towards precious ores and gems, and a device that helps you balance on one leg for 10 seconds if you’re drunk.

lore: There was once a Star Dragon named Gormungandr. Star Dragons are very rare creatures - they sail out amongst the stars, between realms and worlds, reveling in their freedom. But Gormungandr gradually grew bored out there by himself, and flew towards a one world - the world of Krystara - where he thought he might acquaint himself with its Gods.

It turned out that the Gods of Krystara were not too thrilled to see a Star Dragon; after all, they spend a lot of time alone, so when presented with company, they can be quite chatty, imposing, and well… just a little bit annoying. Some Gods, Nysha the Goddess of Magic in particular, took matters in their own hands, and decided to rid themselves of Gormungandr.

Nysha placed a curse on the Star Dragon - a Curse of Hunger. All of a sudden, Gormungandr needed to eat, and eat… and eat. Unable to sail back into the stars where there was so little food, he fell to Krystara, where he began devouring everything in sight. And there he remained, cursed, for many centuries…

lore: Most Lapina are known to be tricksters - their pranks generally involve physical or slapstick humor, often with some real and serious consequences for their targets (deserving OR undeserving). Sonata is a little different though - she is trickster who uses words and music as her medium.

Once, when attending the betrothal party of an Elven Prince, she managed to recite ten verses of the prince’s previous infidelities - all in front of his soon-to-be bride. Were they true? Nobody was sure. But the fact that the slap-mark on the prince’s face left an imprint that lasted a week lent some credence to the idea that his betrothed may actually have already known.

Lately, Sonata has been composing an epic piece - the Ballad of the Burrow - a bawdy and humorous take on the various factions and personalities who inhabit her home kingdom of The Burrows, deep in the Underworld. She tests out small portions of this song on any travelers she meets - some is fit for friends, some is fit for enemies!
